queries: Starbucks shut down AI inventory counting program Reuters miscounted

sources_considered.why: Frames the shutdown as caused by errors, but the page shows no publication date and the claim rests on Reuters.

receipt.public_excerpt: The app – designed to improve ‌Starbucks’ visibility into shortages at stores – frequently miscounted and mislabeled items, such as confusing similar milk types or missing them altogether, Reuters reported in February.

evidence_items.explanation: Confirms the tool was terminated in the week of May 18, 2026, and that it had a documented record of frequent miscounts. This supports the unreliability part.

receipt.public_excerpt: “Thanks for discontinuing Automatic Counting! The thought behind it was great, but the execution was proving difficult,” read one.

evidence_items.explanation: Feedback that Starbucks itself shared points to practical problems with the tool.

receipt.public_excerpt: Starbucks ⁠said the termination of the program – which covered milk and other beverage products – came from a decision to “standardize how inventory is counted across coffeehouses as we continue to focus on consistency and execution at scale.”

evidence_items.explanation: Starbucks's official reason was standardizing its process, not that the tool could not be trusted. This cuts against the stated cause.

unresolved_gaps: No source records Starbucks saying it ended the tool because of inaccuracy. Reuters juxtaposes the errors and the shutdown but does not state the cause.
